transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

Hi. Um... well, I've just been having some trouble at work. I guess what finally pushed me to make an appointment is... well, I'll start working on an EPIC quality report, or I'll sit down in a clinic metrics meeting. And I really intend to pay attention, but... within a few minutes, my mind just drifts off. I end up rereading the same numbers over and over, or I realize I completely missed the whole point of the discussion. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you noticed this kind of trouble concentrating going back to childhood or your school years, or is this something that's really only started recently?

Um... no, I suppose it's not new. It goes back a long time. 

Even back in elementary school, I remember teachers writing that I was bright but... careless. And my mother actually had to sit with me while I finished my homework. I guess I would just lose track of assignments, or forget to bring my books home from school. So... yeah. It's not just recently.
Over the past two weeks or so, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
No... not really. I mean, I get frustrated with work sometimes, but I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or down. Just... normal, I guess.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, health, or family—more days than not, even when there's no clear reason to?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I worry about getting my reports done on time, but... not excessively, I don't think. Just the normal amount of stress.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports chronic, pervasive difficulty sustaining attention (mind wandering during meetings, rereading text, missing key points) beginning in childhood (teacher reports of carelessness, need for parental supervision with homework, losing assignments/books). Symptoms are longstanding, not attributable to a mood or anxiety disorder (depression and GAD screens negative), and cause functional impairment at work, consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation (coded under F90.0 given available candidates).
